title: Case Report: Neonatal lethality caused by novel compound heterozygous missense variants of SLC6A9 gene
abstract: Background                                            The homozygous or compound heterozygous missense variants in the                       SLC6A9                       gene (OMIM*601019) are associated with autosomal recessive glycine encephalopathy with normal serum glycine (OMIM#617301). Fewer than ten                       SLC6A9                       variants have been reported to date. Neonates harboring pathogenic variants in the                       SLC6A9                       gene exhibited a mortality rate of up to 75% during the first 7 months of life. We reported the first documented case of neonate death in China attributable to compound heterozygous missense                       SLC6A9                       variants.                                                                                Methods                                            Trio-based whole-exome sequencing (trio-WES) was performed on genomic DNA (gDNA) of amniotic fluid cells and parental peripheral blood samples. Two mutant                       SLC6A9                       expression vectors, namely pCMV-Flag-Neo(EGFP)-                       SLC6A9                       -m1 and pCMV-Flag-Neo(EGFP)-                       SLC6A9                       -m2 (                       SLC6A9                       -m1/m2), and wild-type pCMV-Flag-Neo(EGFP)-                       SLC6A9                       -wt (                       SLC6A9                       -wt) mammalian expression vectors were constructed. All vectors were subsequently transformed into HEK293T cells. Assays measuring the relative expression of                       SLC6A9                       gene mRNA and SLC6A9 protein were performed. Concurrently, we conducted a systematic review of previously reported                       SLC6A9                       -related cases with accessible clinical data, encompassing relevant genetic testing findings and prenatal/postnatal clinical manifestations.                                                                                Results                                            Trio-WES identified novel compound heterozygous missense variants c.859C &gt; T (p.Arg287Trp) and c.1120T &gt; C (p.Cys374Arg) in the                       SLC6A9                       gene (NM_201649.4).                       In vitro                       functional studies demonstrated that neither variant caused a reduction in the expression of mutant mRNA, but both led to a significant decrease in the expression of mutant SLC6A9 protein. After reviewing the current literature, we found that fetuses with                       SLC6A9                       gene variants commonly presented with increased nuchal translucency (NT), polyhydramnios and talipes equinovarus (clubfoot). Pathogenic                       SLC6A9                       variants exhibited complete penetrance and a relatively consistent phenotypic spectrum characterized by developmental delay, facial dysmorphism, clubfoot, and a high neonatal mortality rate. The characteristic phenotype in affected infants was characterized by elevated cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) glycine concentrations, with or without concurrent elevation in serum glycine levels.                                                                                Conclusion                                            Preliminary evidence from                       in vitro                       functional studies suggested that the pathogenic mechanism of                       SLC6A9                       -related glycine encephalopathy may be associated with the loss-of-function (LoF) effect caused by                       SLC6A9                       gene variants. This study also expanded the mutational spectrum of the                       SLC6A9                       gene.
